rules.title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act (good cause eviction and Notice to Quit requirements)
rules.requirement: A landlord must have good cause to evict a tenant. Each cause except nonpayment of rent must be described in detail in a written notice to the tenant. A Notice to Quit is required for all good cause evictions except nonpayment of rent. A Notice to Cease may also be required as a warning notice, with no statutory time period. A Judgment for Possession must be entered before the tenant must move. For an owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling where the lease has expired, the Notice to Quit is 3 months for at-will or year-to-year tenancies and 1 month for month-to-month tenancies. Rooming and boarding houses must follow the same good cause and notice rules, and the owner must give the County Welfare Board at least 3 working days' notice before starting an eviction action.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit required for all good-cause evictions except nonpayment; 3 months' notice (at-will or year-to-year) or 1 month (month-to-month) for the owner-occupied 2-3 family lease-expiration cause; no statutory period for Notice to Cease

coverage.summary: Statewide good cause eviction rules for residential tenancies; rooming and boarding houses are also covered through DCA regulations. The passages do not state the exempt building types.
